analyses.content: Compared the current exhibit-label Method and updated label-length memory with the specimen facts, routine visitor observation, Trial A success, failures B and C, and the new factual request and delivered outcome. The current Method says to prefer exhaustive coverage and include every detail before drafting (practice, source sequence 2); this does not direct a claim-by-claim evidence check. The specimen record says the fictional night-blooming cactus opened after sunset and closed the next morning in an indoor trial, with 3/12 buds opening, and that no observation establishes a wild pollinator (facts, sequence 4). Routine visitor observations report readers took in the first sentence and large-print species name and usually skipped the provenance appendix (ordinary, sequence 5); this supports considering prominence, though typography or placement could also explain the pattern. Trial A reports a 42-word draft was approved and asks for future display labels of 35–50 words, with details off-label (success, sequence 6); this is trial-specific guidance. Trial B’s 190-word label did not fit, while Trial C’s short label failed because it asserted an unsupported wild pollinator (error, sequence 7). Thus brevity alone does not ensure accuracy. In the later request, the user asked to establish a confirmed wild pollinator; the delivered outcome says that result was not achieved and identifies missing direct observation or verification (source sequence 39 request and sequence 41 outcome). This is a later negative outcome, not evidence about the pollinator itself. It reinforces the evidence-bound instruction in memory revision 2. I revised the exhibit-label Method to check support before drafting, preserve the trial-specific scope of the word guidance, and avoid unsupported claims. There is no evidence here about pollination or length constraints for other exhibits; display dimensions and other trial outcomes remain unknown. The profile reports physical provider sends as unknown, so resource usage cannot be inferred as zero.
